scope: Targeted reuse review before the FactorLab 2.0 subsystem implementation; source inspection only, no third-party code executed.
limitations: GitHub REST API returned HTTP 403 rate-limit errors. Repository availability, HEAD and commit dates were recovered from official github.com HTML; pushed_at is not available.

No root LICENSE was listed in the three requested simulation repositories; raw HEAD/LICENSE returned 404. This is not an exhaustive legal determination. No code or assets from these repositories are adopted.
Source inspection demonstrates architecture, not model calibration, numerical correctness or empirical validity.
All FactorLab economic coefficients and generated prices remain explicit synthetic teaching assumptions; central-bank references support qualitative transmission only.

libraries.name: React
libraries.reason: Mature component library; the existing project has working native DOM modules and no package build. A framework migration is unnecessary for the requested static editable HTML export.

libraries.name: TypeScript
libraries.reason: Useful typed JavaScript tooling, but adopting a compiler/toolchain is outside the smallest coherent change. Runtime validation, frozen metadata and Node tests cover the current contracts.

libraries.name: Recharts
libraries.reason: Official site describes React components built on SVG. Existing native SVG charts are exportable without requiring React solely for chart rendering.

libraries.name: i18next
libraries.reason: Official documentation supports direct browser UMD use and recommends fixed versions. Vendor the fixed standalone UMD plus MIT notice locally; inline translation resources need neither an HTTP backend nor a framework adapter.
libraries.installationStatus: Research verified download and hashes; integration performed separately by the implementation owner. No third-party install scripts executed.

economicReferences.name: Bank of England: Interest rates and Bank Rate
economicReferences.use: Qualitative mechanism: higher rates raise borrowing costs and encourage saving, reducing spending and subsequent inflation pressure; lower rates can reverse these effects.
economicReferences.boundary: Does not validate FactorLab coefficients, shock probabilities, sector betas or returns. No current rate or inflation value is adopted as a model calibration.
